items.text: In VS Code devcontainers and Codespaces, does the agent's shell run inside the app container (no docker CLI) or on a host with Docker, and how do the wp-kit bin/ scripts behave in each case?

survey.reads: wp-kit decisions D-022 and spec sections 3 and 4
survey.where: wp-kit worktree docs/specs/2026-11-22-wp-kit-docker-design.md:159-172,211-217 | evidence: wt-wp-kit .kion/decisions.json D-022; wt-wp-kit docs/specs/2026-11-22-wp-kit-docker-design.md:159-172
survey.result: Decided in wp-kit D-022: the editor and Codespaces attach to a workspace container (devcontainers base image + docker-in-docker) that runs the same root compose.yaml, so the agent shell is NOT inside the app container and has the docker CLI. bin/* always run docker compose exec (with -T when stdin is not a TTY) and never run tools on the host (wp-kit spec 3, Proposal there). In a cloud session the shell runs on the VM with Docker. So in all three places runners stay bin/...; the only in-container case left is a developer who attaches to the app container by hand or a legacy wp-kit devcontainer (attach-to-app, .devcontainer/docker-compose.yml), where docker is absent.

items.text: How does the Compose environment serve HTTPS locally (certificate authority, host names such as *.localhost or a project domain) and how is the CA trusted on WSL2 and Windows browsers?

survey.reads: wp-kit D-012, D-013 and spec Networking; kivo-wise lando-wp wsl2.md
survey.where: wt-wp-kit docs/specs/2026-11-22-wp-kit-docker-design.md:107-121; skills/lando-wp/references/wsl2.md | evidence: wt-wp-kit .kion/decisions.json D-012 D-013; wt-wp-kit docs/specs/2026-11-22-wp-kit-docker-design.md:107-121,219-229; skills/lando-wp/references/wsl2.md (Certificates)
survey.result: HTTPS through the per-project Caddy proxy with 'tls internal' (D-012) on https://<project>.localhost, vite.<project>.localhost and mail.<project>.localhost; host ports from .env (HTTPS_PORT default 443) and bin/setup picks a free port when 443 is busy (D-013). *.localhost resolves to loopback without a hosts entry. bin/trust-cert exports Caddy's root CA (kept in the caddy-data volume) and prints the per-OS trust command; on WSL2 the Windows browsers need the CA imported into the Windows Root store (certutil -addstore -f ROOT <file> from an elevated prompt, reading the file through \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...), Firefox needs security.enterprise_roots.enabled; WSL localhost forwarding makes https://<project>.localhost:<port> reachable from Windows. In Codespaces TLS is terminated by the forwarded URL (*.app.github.dev), not Caddy.

items.text: Which network hosts must a cloud agent session allowlist for a wp-kit project (package registries, plugin marketplace, docs hosts, container registries) and which secrets arrive as proxy-injected network secrets (for example private Composer repositories)?

survey.reads: cloud environments doc: default allowed domains, network secrets, what is available; wp-kit spec 4 allowlist and D-014
survey.where: public documentation; wt-wp-kit spec section 4 | evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#default-allowed-domains; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#add-network-secrets; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments (What's available in cloud sessions table); wt-wp-kit .kion/decisions.json D-014 D-019
survey.result: Default allowlist (Limited + Allow package managers) already covers github.com, raw/objects.githubusercontent.com, registry-1.docker.io, auth.docker.io, production.cloudflare.docker.com, ghcr.io, mcr.microsoft.com, packagist.org, repo.packagist.org, registry.npmjs.org, Ubuntu archives, nodejs.org. Not on it and needed by a wp-kit project: wpackagist.org, api.wordpress.org, downloads.wordpress.org, connect.advancedcustomfields.com (ACF Pro), pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com (ghcr blob downloads), plus docs hosts for the corpus fallback (developer.wordpress.org, roots.io, docs.docker.com, containers.dev). Network secrets: the agent proxy attaches the secret to requests for the listed hosts after they leave the VM; it never enters the VM; never attached to GitHub, the Anthropic API or public registries (registry.npmjs.org etc.). ACF Pro Composer access is the one secret (wp-kit D-014: network secret for connect.advancedcustomfields.com; Username and password type). Environment variables are readable by every user: no secret there. Marketplaces declared in a repository's settings (extraKnownMarketplaces) are NOT added in Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions; committed .claude/skills|agents|commands, hooks in .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json are. Status: documented; cloud probe pending (dev/probes/environment-probe.sh) for the non-default hosts and the Composer basic-auth behaviour through the proxy.

grounds: parallel work: mysql:8.4 failed to start with the installed recipe because of expire_logs_days
items.text: Does the Lando mysql service at the installed recipe version write expire_logs_days into its my.cnf, which MySQL 8.4 removed, and what override fixes it?

survey.reads: installed Lando wordpress recipe config files and the upstream recipe corpus
survey.result: Yes. With Lando v3.26.9 the wordpress recipe's default database config ~/.lando/config/wordpress/mysql8.cnf (marker LANDOWORDPRESSMYSQL8CNF, used for every mysql:8.x) sets 'expire_logs_days = 10' at line 51; MySQL 8.4 removed that variable, so mysqld aborts on the unknown option and the database service never becomes healthy. Upstream lando/wordpress main (6d07797, 2026-10-15) fixed it: its wordpress-mysql84 example asserts binlog_expire_logs_seconds=864000 instead of the removed expire_logs_days, and the mysql:8 alias resolves to 8.4 there. Fixes: (a) database: mysql:8.0; (b) config.config.database pointing at a project file — the builder uses it INSTEAD of the default (getServiceConfig only falls back to defaultFiles when the key is absent), so it must be a full copy of mysql8.cnf with expire_logs_days replaced by binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 864000; (c) a Lando release that bundles the fixed recipe.
